newsitem.title: UK: UK unemployment may fall to 5 pct by 2000-report.
newsitem.headline: UK unemployment may fall to 5 pct by 2000-report.

text.p: Britain will be one of the few countries to achieve the European Union objective, set in 1993, to halve unemployment by the year 2000, a report commissioned by the European Commission said on Monday.
The Centre for Economic Performance added Britain's unemployment rate may fall to five percent or lower. It was 6.7 percent in December.
"Falling UK unemployment since 1993 is the product of some successful supply side-reforms and expansionary macroeconomic policy," the CEP report said.
It said labour market deregulation was not the main reason behind the fall.
The CEP said pay determination was the only area to undergo extensive deregulation in the UK, with industrial relations legislation playing a greater role where it had previously been limited.

"Also in the field of individual employment rights there has been no overall trend towards greater deregulation: the UK labour market was already less regulated than many other European countries in 1979," the report said.
It said the widening wage and income inequality in the UK over the 1980s and concluded it was an issue yet to be resolved.
